long_biography.plain_text:
When his family's camera chain faced liquidation, David Ritz assembled a rescue bid with money from relatives and outside investors. After an auction that lasted almost a day, he returned to headquarters to find employees waiting outside to applaud him. Their welcome moved him to tears.

The rescue also demanded a different approach to photography. Ritz's stores began selling televisions, netbooks and mobile phones, while offering memory cards and DVDs that let customers watch photographs and video clips together. He acknowledged that the business could no longer assume customers would keep paying for printed pictures. The recovery proved temporary: another bankruptcy ended with the stores and online operations sold to new owners in 2012.
